title: Cache-key taxonomy and hit-decay modeling for safe rollforward
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce a taxonomy of cache keys and a hit-decay model that informs per-key TTL suggestions, staged rollout thresholds, and automatic rollback triggers. Deliverables: (1) cache-key taxonomy document mapping common request shapes to key families and their expected access patterns; (2) hit-decay simulation harness that takes historical prefix traces and outputs expected hit-rate over time under various TTL ladders and soft-eviction policies; (3) a safe rollout plan (canary -> cohorted ramp -> global) with concrete metric thresholds and automated rollback conditions; (4) instrumentation additions (prefix-level counters, cohort sampling) and a small PR to the config applier to support staged TTL ladders and shadow dry-runs.
comments: 2025-01-09 — Kickoff: scoped deliverables with PM (R. Chen) and Design (L. Park). Agreed to prioritize taxonomy for the top 25% of traffic prefixes by QPS and build a simulator for historical traces.

2025-01-14 — Data pull: exported 30 days of prefix traces from staging and prod (query ids anonymized). Initial EDA shows two dominant shapes: short-lived conversational prefixes (high burst, steep decay) and long-lived background prefixes (low churn, stable hits). Noted significant variance in per-customer key cardinality.

2025-01-20 — Prototype simulator complete (python). Simulator models: exponential hit-decay curves, TTL ladder application, soft-eviction (age-weighted), and inter-request batching effects. Ran baseline on sample trace: applying a single static TTL (60s) increased cost by 17% for high-cardinality keys; TTL ladder reduced cost with negligible latency impact in canary cohort.

2025-01-24 — Design review: presented taxonomy UI mock to Console team — idea to surface recommended TTLs and a preview of expected hit-rate/time series before applying. UX requested a confidence score and a one-click ‘shadow apply’ toggle.

2025-01-28 — Eng sync: defined rollout stages: shadow -> 1% cohort -> 10% cohort -> 50% -> 100%. Agreed on metric suite: prefix hit-rate delta, miss-rate QPS, p95 token latency, model throughput utilization, and cost-per-1M-tokens. Added automated rollback conditions: any >8% regression in prefix hit-rate with correlated >5% cost increase in cohort window, or p95 latency increase >15%.

2025-02-03 — Bench results: ran canary on internal staging cluster. Observed expected small hit-rate uplift for background prefixes and minor degradation for ephemeral conversational prefixes when aggressive TTL applied. Adjusted TTL ladder for ephemeral keys to include decay curve instead of fixed TTL (adaptive TTL = base_ttl * decay_factor(current_hour_activity)).

2025-02-07 — Security and privacy check: confirmed key taxonomy will not include PII; all sampled keys are hashed and cardinality-only metrics exported. Security advised adding a config flag to prevent external exports of sample payloads.

2025-02-10 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521 — implements prefix-level counters, cohort assignment tags, and a dry-run mode in the config applier. Requesting review from @samira and @yuri for kernel-safety and infra cost impacts.

2025-02-12 — PM review: Paula (PM) approved canary plan pending two changes: (1) add economic budget governor that prevents TTL rollout if projected cost saving < $500/month for the tenant; (2) ensure console shows pre-apply simulation and historical cohort comparisons. Blocking tasks assigned to UX and billing integration.
